newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman, Japan sign new minerals exploration pact.
newsitem.headline: Oman, Japan sign new minerals exploration pact.

text.p: Oman's Ministry of Petroleum and Minerals on Tuesday signed an agreement with Japan to explore for minerals in northern Oman, an official said.

Director General of Minerals Mohammed Kassim al-Yafai said the agreement was "based on the technical cooperation agreement between the Oman government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency and the Metal Mining Agency of Japan".

Under the deal, the Japanese team would spend $4 million on surveying and exploring for copper, gold and silver and other minerals in a 2,900 square km area on the Batina coast between Rustaq and Saham, Yafai told Reuters.
He said the three-year project would start in August. Three feasibility studies on the mining potential of the surveyed blocks would be prepared during the project.
In 1995, Japan and Oman signed a similar exploration pact.
